subject: Order form: ramp schedule, escrow holdback & withholding — net30 proposal
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@priorihealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form commercial questions (ramp / tax / invoicing)

Hi Evelyn / Ben,

Thanks for the draft — quick clarifying questions from procurement before we move to legal:
- PrioriHealth expects Net45 on invoices for enterprise deals. Can Redwood confirm flexibility to Net45?
- We have an internal withholding policy for certain international entity payments. If PrioriHealth has to withhold tax, will Redwood accept withholding (i.e., reduce invoice) or do you require gross-up?
- One of our controllers asked whether activation fees can be prorated to the first full month of service rather than upfront.

Attached a short checklist from our AP team. If we can get these items confirmed, I can route the order form to legal and procurement for signature.

Best,
Maria
Maria Lopez
Head of Procurement, PrioriHealth
+1 415-555-0123

Attachments: procurement_checklist.pdf

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@priorihealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form commercial questions (ramp / tax / invoicing)

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear checklist. Quick responses below and attaching an updated order form (v3) with the changes we think address your asks.

1) Net terms: Redwood standard is Net30, but we can accommodate Net45 for enterprise customers with a slight change to billing cadence in the order form. For this deal (RDW-4521) Ben and I propose keeping Net30 but offering Net45 as a concession tied to an activation escrow holdback (5% of each invoice) for the first 3 months. That helps preserve predictability on our side while meeting PrioriHealth cashflow needs.

2) Withholding: We can accept customer withholding where local law requires it, provided PrioriHealth supplies a valid withholding certificate and the invoice reflects the net amount withheld. Alternatively, we can include a ‘gross-up’ clause in the order form if PrioriHealth prefers Redwood to receive the full contracted amount — open to discuss.

3) Activation fee proration: We are open to prorating activation fees to the first full month rather than charging immediately; updated language in v3 covers prorated activation.

Next steps: Ben — can you confirm commercial approval for the 5% escrow holdback proposal? Kimberly — can Legal review the attached redlines on withholding and escrow language (MSA ref: Section 4.2 / Order Form Appendix A)? Maria — if this direction works, I can route v3 to DocuSign (linked) and loop in accounting for invoice remit entity.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Priori_OrderForm_v3.pdf
Related: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/rdw-4521

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 12:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form commercial questions (ramp / tax / invoicing)

Eve — fine with the Net30 + temporary escrow holdback approach as a negotiating compromise. A couple of commercial notes:
- Recommend escrow holdback of 5% per invoice for first 90 days post-go-live, released on acceptance of monthly usage reports (Customer sign-off).
- If PrioriHealth pushes strictly for Net45 without holdback we should ask for a 1.5% uplift on list pricing to offset financing impact.

Kimberly — can Legal flag any regulatory issues with the release conditions? Also confirm whether the withholding language should require a certificate AND a reference to the specific taxing jurisdiction in the invoice.

If Maria is okay with v3 we should get DocuSign going today to keep timeline.

— Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form commercial questions (ramp / tax / invoicing)

Ben / Eve — reading through v3 and the proposed commercial approach. Suggested legal redline language below — will paste into the order form appendix and MSA cross-ref: 

"Withholding and Tax. Customer may withhold taxes from payments to Redwood only to the extent required by applicable law. Customer shall provide Redwood with appropriate official documentation (e.g., withholding certificate) issued by the relevant tax authority within thirty (30) days of the invoice date. If Customer withholds taxes in excess of amounts required by law or fails to timely provide documentation, Redwood reserves the right to (a) require the Customer to remit the gross amount and provide evidence of payment to the tax authority, or (b) charge an additional fee to offset the administrative and financial impact of withholding. Any tax gross-up requested by Customer must be agreed in writing in the applicable Order Form."
Two additional asks for Finance/Accounting:
- Please confirm the remit entity for PrioriHealth invoices (we need the legal entity + tax id). If PrioriHealth intends to pay from a non-US entity, we should evaluate treaty/withholding implications.
- For the escrow release condition, clarify whether customer sign-off is acceptable or if we need an independent acceptance test (I suggest customer sign-off with an escalation path).

I can pre-populate the redline in DocuSign if you want me to. Attaching a withholding_certificate_template for their AP team.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: withholding_certificate_template.pdf

From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@priorihealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@priorihealth.com>, PrioriHealth Procurement <procurement@priorihealth.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form commercial questions (ramp / tax / invoicing)

Evelyn / Ben / Kimberly — appreciate the quick turnaround and the clarifications. A few confirmations from our side:
- PrioriHealth can accept Net30 provided Redwood removes the 1.5% uplift ask. Our preference had been Net45, but we can move to Net30 if the escrow holdback language is time-limited to 90 days and releases on receipt of the monthly usage acceptance (we will not gate acceptance for trivial disputes).
- We will provide the required withholding certificate if any withholding is applied and will identify the paying entity + tax ID on the PO.
- Activation fee: agreed to prorate to first full month — please reflect in the final order form.

Please proceed with final redline in DocuSign and route to Samir (CFO) for signature. I will upload the withholding certificate template where our AP team can complete it.

Thanks,
Maria Lopez
Head of Procurement, PrioriHealth
